title: Compliance Bulletin: One Medicare Supplement Policy at a Time, and the Replacement It Requires
content:
A member may hold only one Medicare Supplement policy at a time, because selling a second supplement to someone who already holds one is a duplicate policy and is not permitted. The maximum number of policies under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies a member may hold at one time is 1.

### The condition on taking an application

No other Medicare Supplement policy is already in force for this member, standing as active or in its grace period, on the day the new policy would take effect. The condition is settled before the application is recorded, and it is settled from the plan's own records of the member's supplement policies — the policies held for that member, the status each stands at, the day each took effect and the plan letter each carries — correlated to the applicant by the member the application is being taken for. What the applicant says about the policies they hold is not what decides it.

### Where the member already holds one

Where the member already holds one, the new application is taken only as a replacement: the applicant signs the replacement notice, the old policy ends the day before the new one begins, and no day is covered twice or left uncovered.

### Policies that are no bar

A policy that has already lapsed, been cancelled or been rescinded is no bar to a new application, and an applicant's history may show several ended policies.

### Positive and negative cases

Take a hypothetical applicant whose record shows one supplement standing as active on the day the new policy would take effect. That is another policy in force, so the new application is taken only as a replacement, on the terms above.

Take instead a hypothetical applicant whose record shows two supplements, both ended — one lapsed and one cancelled. Neither stands as active nor in its grace period, so neither is a bar, and the application is taken in the ordinary way.

An applicant who says they want to keep both policies is told plainly why they cannot, and that paying two supplement premiums would buy them nothing.
